name: AT24C256
full_name: Atmel/Microchip AT24C256 256Kbit (32K x 8) I2C Two-Wire Serial EEPROM
description: The AT24C256 is Atmel's (now Microchip's) 256 Kbit (32,768 x 8) two-wire serial EEPROM, the direct competitor and pin-for-pin equivalent of the 24LC256. It operates from 2.7V to 5.5V (1.8V low-voltage variants exist), supports 400 kHz at 5V, and uses a 64-byte page write buffer. Three address pins permit eight devices on one I2C bus. Endurance is one million write cycles with multi-decade retention. Its standout trait is drop-in interchangeability with the Microchip 24LC256 in nearly every design.

pins.name: WP
pins.description: write protect; high write-protects upper half/whole array depending on variant

typical_application: Storing settings, lookup tables, or serial-number data for embedded systems over I2C.
gotchas: requires external pull-ups on SDA and SCL like any I2C device
WP on some die revisions protects only the upper half of the array, not the whole device; check the exact revision datasheet
1.8V variants (AT24C256...-1.8) exist; the standard part is 2.7V minimum, so verify before running at 2.5V
tie A0-A2 to defined levels; floating address pins cause unreliable addressing
use acknowledge polling after writes, the device NAKs while the internal write is in progress
page-write rollover within the 64-byte page can silently corrupt data if you write across a boundary
